claims.text: The initial HEA is intended for use as an intermediate material in plasma-facing reactor components.
The initial HEA composition excludes high-thermal-conductivity elements such as Cu or Ag.
The proposed intervention is to add 5–10 at% Cu or Ag to the HEA.
Cu or Ag atoms will remain dispersed in the HEA matrix.
Solid-solution strengthening will be maintained after adding Cu or Ag.
Entropy stabilization will maintain phase stability after adding Cu or Ag.
Adding Cu or Ag will increase electronic thermal conductivity because these elements have high intrinsic conductivity.
Entropy stabilization will prevent significant phase segregation caused by the Cu or Ag addition.
Entropy stabilization will prevent significant embrittlement caused by the Cu or Ag addition.
The Cu- or Ag-modified HEA will have at least 20% higher thermal conductivity than the baseline HEA.
The Cu or Ag addition will reduce yield strength by less than 10% relative to the baseline HEA.
The Cu or Ag addition will reduce ductility by less than 10% relative to the baseline HEA.
The predicted improvements and property retention will hold at temperatures up to 800°C.
The predicted improvements and property retention will hold under tensile or compressive stresses up to the material's yield strength.
The predicted improvements and property retention will hold in vacuum or an inert atmosphere.
Cu or Ag fractions exceeding the solubility limit or causing precipitation may degrade structural integrity.
Additions of no more than 10 at% Cu or Ag constitute a moderate regime in which the hypothesis is expected to hold.
The baseline HEA has moderate thermal conductivity and high structural integrity.
